summary: Halliday, Arthur and the narrator negotiate terms with the Feds (NSA/DHS) over Halliday's mathematical proof, which is still missing and uncontained. Their demands include protection for Halliday with no government oversight of the writing process, no charges against anyone involved, and freedom to speak without surveillance. The Feds refuse to let the group keep a copy of the proof, and the narrator plans to write it out later anyway. The Feds then set up a safe house for Halliday at an abandoned mountain estate, with the NSA controlling access from a distance while Arthur and the narrator can move in and out.
one_line: Halliday, Arthur and the narrator bargain with the NSA and DHS over terms for Halliday's proof and a mountain safe house.
key_facts: Halliday says the group should present demands and make a deal quickly so the NSA has the mathematical information needed to prevent attacks.
Arthur says of the government: "They ain't the bad guys."
The narrator demands to protect Halliday personally, with no NSA or DHS looking over her shoulder while she writes the proof.
Arthur demands that no charges be brought against any of the people involved.
The group insists on keeping a copy of the proof so the information can get out if they are killed.
The narrator demands freedom to speak without spying and says they will bring their own tech to check for it.
The Feds refuse to let the group keep a copy of the proof, claiming they do not trust them to keep it secure.
The Feds argue that the security overhaul would make the group no longer a threat, so they have no need for leverage.
The narrator accepts the refusal because they could write the proof out themselves afterward without the Feds being able to stop them.
The Feds set up a safe house for Halliday in the mountains.
The safe house is an abandoned estate that is old but clean and in good repair.
The NSA sets up at a respectful distance and controls access to the house.
Arthur and the narrator have freedom to move in and out of the safe house.
The proof is still missing and uncontained, so Halliday will help propagate security overhauls everywhere.
